title: The Amazing Spider-Man
synopsis: Peter Parker investigates his father’s work, develops unusual powers and faces a threat created by Dr. Connors’s research.
verdictRationale: Peter’s attention shifts from retaliation to rescue. The change gives families a worthwhile discussion even as early vigilantism is played for laughs.
ageRationale: A bridge rescue, frightening reptilian transformations, fatal violence and suggestive remarks make this a teen recommendation.
reflection: Peter initially wields power to make people feel small. His growing attentiveness to strangers opens an Orthodox discussion about the difference between ability and the patient love that should govern it.

title: The Wolverine
synopsis: Logan travels to Japan and protects Mariko while a former acquaintance seeks his healing ability.
verdictRationale: Care for Mariko gives Logan purpose beyond his isolation. Prolonged and sometimes graphic combat tempers the positive example.
ageRationale: Repeated lethal claw attacks, injury, strong language and implied sex support a 16+ recommendation for the theatrical cut.
reflection: Logan’s grief makes isolation understandable. His return to caring for someone gives families a way to discuss how accepting help and seeking companionship can renew a sense of responsibility.

title: The Amazing Spider-Man 2
synopsis: Peter tries to protect Gwen while Max Dillon and Harry Osborn become dangerous adversaries.
verdictRationale: Peter’s defense of others is admirable, but a tragic loss and repeated coercion complicate the example. The film gives families material for a conversation about listening before trying to decide for someone.
ageRationale: Electro is tortured, several scenes involve painful transformations, and the climax includes a traumatic death. The film also includes profanity and drinking.
reflection: Peter’s fear for Gwen is real. Families can ask how concern becomes more constructive when it makes room for another person’s judgment, gifts and responsibilities.

title: X-Men: Days of Future Past
synopsis: Surviving mutants send Logan’s consciousness back to 1973 to prevent a future of coordinated extermination.
verdictRationale: Raven’s decision to spare a life shows that people can interrupt a cycle of retaliation. Graphic fantasy violence and the nudity and drinking advisories still matter.
ageRationale: Sentinels impale and kill mutants. Rear nudity, heavy drinking and strong profanity support 13+ for the original theatrical cut.
reflection: Xavier’s hope takes the form of trust that Raven can choose differently. An Orthodox conversation can dwell on repentance as a real change of direction even after many choices have narrowed the path.

title: Logan
synopsis: An ill Logan cares for Charles Xavier and reluctantly escorts Laura, a child pursued by people who engineered her abilities.
verdictRationale: Logan’s protection of Laura and his care for Xavier carry real moral weight. The draft weighs sustained graphic killing and the repeated use of children in brutal combat as dominant concerns for family viewing.
ageRationale: The original R-rated film includes graphic dismemberment, pervasive strong profanity, brief toplessness and heavy drinking. Recommend adults only.
reflection: Logan expects little good from companionship. The meal offered by the farm family briefly gives him an image of hospitality, and his relationship with Laura later requires him to accept responsibility he had tried to avoid.

biblicalParallels.title: Taking responsibility after misplaced trust
biblicalParallels.filmMoment: Peter gives Beck access to Stark’s technology and then takes responsibility for stopping its misuse.
biblicalParallels.reflection: Paul’s teaching helps frame the difference between wanting relief and considering who might be harmed by handing a decision to someone else. Peter’s repair starts when classmates’ safety becomes his focus.

questions: What does Peter want from his trip?
Why does Beck seem trustworthy at first?
Which clue helps MJ discover what is happening?
What does Peter do after admitting he misjudged Beck?
How can your family check an impressive video before believing or sharing it?

findings: Peter is seen partly undressed while changing suits, and teenagers kiss.
The guide reports profanity and suggestive banter.
Drone attacks, explosions and threatening illusions put students and bystanders in danger.
An apparent elemental attack damages a church tower. A chaperone suggests witches as an explanation.
Beck drinks beer while Peter has lemonade. Another teenager tries to accept an alcoholic drink.
Beck manufactures false dangers, and Peter works to protect his classmates after handing him access.
